source_text:
Οὐκ οἴομαι δέ, ὅτι μικρὰν συμβουλίαν ἐποιησάμην περὶ ἐγκρατείας, ἣν ποιήσας τις οὐ μετανοήσει, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἑαυτὸν σώσει κἀμὲ τὸν συμβουλεύσαντα. μισθὸς γὰρ οὔκ ἐστιν μικρὸς πλανωμένην ψυχὴν καὶ ἀπολλυμένην ἀποστρέψαι εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι.
ταύτην γὰρ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἀποδοῦναι τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι ἡμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ λέγων καὶ ἀκούων μετὰ πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ λέγῃ καὶ ἀκούῃ.
ἐμμείνωμεν οὖν ἐφ̓ οἷς ἐπιστεύσαμεν δίκαιοι καὶ ὅσιοι, ἵνα μετὰ παρρησίας αἰτῶμεν τὸν θεὸν τὸν λέγοντα: Ἔτι λαλοῦντός σου ἐρῶ: ἰδοὺ πάρειμι.
τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ ῥῆμα μεγάλης ἐστιν ἐπαγγελίας σημεῖον: ἑτοιμότερον γὰρ ἑαυτὸν λέγει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸ διδόναι τοῦ αἰτοῦντος.
τοσαύτης οὖν χρηστότητος μεταλαμβάνοντες μὴ φθονήσωμεν ἑαυτοῖς τυχεῖν τοσούτων ἀγαθῶν. ὅσην γὰρ ἡδονὴν ἔχει τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα τοῖς ποιήσασιν αὐτά, τοσαύτην κατάκρισιν ἔχει τοῖς παρακούσασιν.
thought_title: The reward of counsel and the promise of God's readiness
orientation: The preacher has just finished urging the congregation to keep the flesh pure, and now he reflects on the value of his own counsel about self-control and the reward for turning a straying soul back to salvation.
pass_a_gloss: I do not think that I made small counsel about self-control, which if someone does, he will not repent, but he will both save himself and me the one who counseled. For the reward is not small to turn back a wandering and perishing soul to be saved. For this recompense we have to give back to God who created us, if the one speaking and the one hearing with faith and love both speaks and hears. Let us remain then in what we believed, righteous and holy, so that with boldness we may ask God who says: While you are still speaking I will say: Behold, I am here. For this word is a sign of great promise: for the Lord says he is more ready to give than the one asking. Sharing then in such great kindness, let us not begrudge ourselves to obtain such great good things. For as much pleasure as these words have for those who have done them, so much condemnation they have for those who have disobeyed.

choices.why: The noun denotes advice or exhortation, matching the homiletic context of the preacher's appeal.
The glossary fixes this term as 'recompense' for the return given to God or received from him.
The word denotes confident, open speech before God, fitting the context of asking with assurance.
The comparative adjective describes God's greater readiness to give than the one asking, preserving the comparison.
The verb means to envy or begrudge, and the hortatory subjunctive with μή preserves the negative exhortation.

bible_refs.note: Ἔτι λαλοῦντός σου ἐρῶ: ἰδοὺ πάρειμι

pass_b_english: I do not think I have given you small counsel about self-control. The one who follows it will not regret it. He will save himself, and he will save me as well, the one who gave the counsel. For it is no small reward to turn back a wandering and perishing soul so that it may be saved.
This is the recompense we are able to give to the God who created us: that the one who speaks and the one who hears should both speak and hear with faith and love.
Let us then remain in what we believed, righteous and holy, so that we may ask God with boldness. For he says, "While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am" (Isaiah 65:24).
This word is a sign of a great promise, for the Lord says that he is readier to give than the one who asks is to ask.

Since we share in such great kindness, let us not begrudge ourselves the chance to obtain such great good things. For as much pleasure as these words hold for those who do them, so much condemnation do they hold for those who refuse to listen.

problems.quote: he is more ready to give than the one who asks
problems.source_quote: ἑτοιμότερον γὰρ ἑαυτὸν λέγει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸ διδόναι τοῦ αἰτοῦντος
problems.why: Greek says 'readier to give than the one who asks is [ready] to ask' or 'readier to give than the asker is to ask', not 'more ready to give than the one who asks'. The comparison is between God's readiness to give and the asker's readiness to ask, not God's giving vs. the asker's asking.
problems.fix: for the Lord says that he is readier to give than the one who asks is to ask
problems.ruling: τοῦ αἰτοῦντος is genitive comparison: 'readier to give than the asker is to ask'; English 'more ready to give than the one who asks' is ambiguous/misleading.

edits.old: for the Lord says that he is more ready to give than the one who asks.
edits.new: for the Lord says that he is readier to give than the one who asks is to ask.

problems.quote: While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am
problems.why: Isaiah 65:24 reads 'Before they call I will answer; while they are yet speaking I will hear,' not 'Here I am.'
problems.fix: Note this is a paraphrase or variant rendering of Isaiah 65:24.

edits.old: For he says, "While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am" (Isaiah 65:24).
edits.new: For he says, "While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am" (compare Isaiah 65:24).

fixed: The scripture citation was corrected to indicate that the quotation is a paraphrase or variant rendering of Isaiah 65:24, not a direct quotation.

problems.quote: While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am
problems.why: No biblical reference is given; this is from Isaiah 65:24 ('before they call I will answer; while they are yet speaking I will hear').

variants.text: While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am

edits.old: For he says, "While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am."
edits.new: For he says, "While you are still speaking, I will say: Here I am" (Isaiah 65:24).

fixed: Added Isaiah 65:24 reference to the quotation, as the source quotes Isaiah 65:24 and the brief requires modern citations for Scripture.

last_rejected.why: Brief bans 'reward' for ἀντιμισθία; μισθὸς here is related and should use 'recompense'.
last_rejected.fix: For it is no small recompense to turn back a wandering and perishing soul so that it may be saved.
last_rejected.ruling: μισθὸς and ἀντιμισθία are distinct words; 'reward' is standard for μισθὸς (e.g., Matt 5:12, 1 Cor 9:17).

last_rejected.quote: he will save himself, and he will save me as well, the one who gave the counsel
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἑαυτὸν σώσει κἀμὲ τὸν συμβουλεύσαντα
last_rejected.why: Source says 'but also' (ἀλλὰ καὶ), implying more than just no regret; English drops the adversative 'but also'.
last_rejected.fix: but he will also save himself and me, the one who gave the counsel
last_rejected.ruling: ἀλλὰ καὶ commonly means 'but also/nay even' intensifying; English 'will not regret it; he will save...' captures the progression adequately.

last_rejected.why: English 'he says' obscures that God is the one speaking; source has 'the God who says' with participial phrase.
last_rejected.ruling: Prior clause 'ask God' identifies speaker; 'he says' naturally refers to God. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: he is readier to give than the one who asks is to ask
last_rejected.source_quote: ἑτοιμότερον γὰρ ἑαυτὸν λέγει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸ διδόναι τοῦ αἰτοῦντος
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'readier himself to give than the one asking'—meaning God is readier to give than the asker is to ask; English garbles this as 'readier to give than... is to ask' which is unclear and slightly misrepresents the comparison structure.
last_rejected.fix: the Lord says he is readier himself to give than the asker is to ask
last_rejected.ruling: 'Readier to give than the one who asks is to ask' correctly renders εἰς τὸ διδόναι τοῦ αἰτοῦντος; comparison is clear.

last_rejected.quote: begrudge ourselves the chance to obtain
last_rejected.why: φθονέω means 'envy, begrudge' with dative; 'begrudge ourselves' is odd—better 'deny ourselves' or 'grudge ourselves' the obtaining. The sense is 'let us not deprive ourselves of obtaining.'
last_rejected.fix: let us not deny ourselves the obtaining of
last_rejected.ruling: φθονήσωμεν ἑαυτοῖς τυχεῖν = 'begrudge ourselves obtaining'; standard idiom. 'Chance to obtain' is minor paraphrase, not error.

polish.changed: Removed the incorrect Isaiah 65:24 reference, clarified the speaker of the quoted promise as God, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud.
